Compute the small-world index of a network

Source: R/graph_metrics.R
net_smallworld.Rd

net_smallworld() computes the small-world index sigma of a network. A small-world network combines the high clustering of a regular lattice with the short paths between nodes of a random graph, and Humphries and Gurney (2008) quantify this with sigma: the transitivity of the network relative to that of comparable random graphs, divided by its average shortest-path length relative to theirs, sigma = (C / C_rand) / (L / L_rand). A value of sigma above 1 indicates small-world structure.

The function computes the index on the unweighted network, in which an edge is present when its weight is nonzero, and compares it with n_rand random graphs that keep the degree of every node, obtained by rewiring pairs of edges. Because the reference graphs are random, the result varies between calls unless seed is given.

It returns one row with sigma, the transitivity and average shortest-path length of the network, and their means over the random graphs.

For the clustering of each node, use net_clustering().

Usage

net_smallworld(x, n_rand = 100L, seed = NULL)

Arguments

x

An undirected fitted network (psychnet) or a symmetric weighted adjacency matrix.

n_rand

Number of random reference graphs. Default 100.

seed

Optional seed for the random graphs. The caller's random number stream is restored afterwards. Default NULL (the current stream).

Value

A one-row data frame of class psychnet_smallworld, with columns smallworldness (sigma; NA when undefined), transitivity, aspl (average shortest-path length), and transitivity_rand and aspl_rand (their means over the random graphs).

Details

Transitivity is the global clustering coefficient: three times the number of triangles divided by the number of connected triples. The average shortest-path length is taken over the pairs of nodes joined by a path. The index is undefined when the random graphs have no triangles or no paths.

Conditions

psychnet_bad_input when x is directed, is not a finite symmetric square matrix of at least two nodes, or n_rand is not a positive whole number; psychnet_undefined_statistic (warning) when the random graphs have no triangles or no paths, so that sigma is NA.

References

Humphries, M. D., & Gurney, K. (2008). Network 'small-world-ness': A quantitative method for determining canonical network equivalence. PLoS ONE, 3(4), e0002051. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0002051

See also

net_clustering() for clustering per node.

Examples

S <- 0.4^abs(outer(1:8, 1:8, "-"))
net_smallworld(ebic_glasso(cor_matrix = S, n = 400), n_rand = 50, seed = 1)
#>   smallworldness transitivity aspl transitivity_rand aspl_rand
#> 1              0            0    3              0.04  2.735769
